ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly high-contrast distribution with approximately 65% high-intensity (white) pixels in the inner lobes and 35% low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels along the margins and peduncle base.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-intensity white fields occupying the interior of both lobes; thick black border along the entire trailing edge and outer tips; dense dark mottling and vertical streaking concentrated at the junction of the lobes and extending from the peduncle base.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped notch with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 42 degrees and a depth-to-width ratio indicating significant penetration into the central fluke mass.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Irregularly serrated continuous boundary; high-frequency, low-amplitude peaks (3-6 pixel amplitude) along the primary trailing edge, with more pronounced jaggedness observed on the distal outer edges.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strong convex curve extending from the median notch to the mid-lobe, transitioning into a slight concavity (recurve) near the lateral terminal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Clusters of high-contrast white circular pixel clusters (likely barnacle colonization or scars) visible on the extreme lateral margins of both the left and right lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Extensive dark, unaligned linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) traversing the high-intensity white fields; particularly prominent diagonal streaks on the right lobe and vertical streaks on the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Multiple parallel linear scars (rake marks) across the ventral surface; dark pigmentation anomalies at the base of the fluke near the peduncle attachment.
other_distinctive_markers: A distinct vertical dark-pigmented 'smear' or 'drip' pattern originating from the central lower margin and extending upward into the white field of the left lobe.
